chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Amr ibn Uthman, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Mus'ab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Three traditions were established regarding Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur al-Ansari. As for the first of them: The people used to clean themselves with stones, so Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur ate pumpkin (daba'), his stomach softened (became loose), and he cleaned himself with water. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed regarding this: 'Indeed, Allah loves those who turn to Him in repentance and loves those who purify themselves.' Thus, the tradition of cleaning with water was established.

When death approached him, he was absent from Medina, so he ordered that his face be turned towards the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He willed one-third of his wealth. Thus, the verse of inheritance was revealed regarding the Qibla (direction), and the tradition of the one-third share was established.

key_terms.الدباء: A type of pumpkin or gourd
key_terms.القبلة: The direction of prayer (here referring to the context of revelation or orientation)

ai.seo_question: What are the three traditions established by Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights how the actions of Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur established three key Sunnas: the preference for water over stones for istinja' (purification), the orientation towards the Prophet during death, and the legal limit of one-third for bequests. Notably, the verse 'Indeed, Allah loves those who repent and those who purify themselves' (2:222) is cited as the divine confirmation of the purification practice, linking physical cleanliness to spiritual devotion in Shia jurisprudence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-267 Ahmad ibn Zyad ibn Ja’far al-Hamedany - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Amr ibn Uthman, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Mus’ab that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“Three traditions were ascribed to Al-Bara’ ibn Ma’rur al-Ansari . The people used to clean themselves up with stones when they went to the toilet. Once Al-Bara’ ibn Ma’rur had eaten a lot of pumpkin so he got diarrhea and washed himself with water after going to the toilet. Then the Honorable the Exalted God revealed the following verse, ‘…For Allah loves those who turn to Him constantly and He loves those who keep themselves pure and clean.’ Thereafter, washing up with water after going to the toilet became established as a tradition.

Al-Bara’ ibn Ma’rur al-Ansari was outside Medina when he was about to pass away. He asked that he be turned facing the Prophet (MGB) who was in Medina, and willed that one-third of his inheritance be spent in charity. Thus, these three acts became established traditions.”
